probes.name: PA0
probes.subject: tools/absent.py
probes.note: Instrument control (Lesson #0056). Every T-ABSENT reading in the module is parsed from this report line; change its spacing and the argv-with-no-shell run can no longer be read back. The control must be able to go RED before any rendered reading is trusted.

probes.name: PA1
probes.subject: tools/goal_template.py
probes.note: 🔴 C0's --pattern restored to repr. The control value carries a backslash, which repr doubles and bash single quotes keep doubled: the s295 mechanism, on the control check.

probes.name: PA2
probes.subject: tools/goal_template.py
probes.note: C0's --control restored to repr: the one C0 site PA1 leaves quoted. The escaped-paren control arrives as a different but still valid regex, finds nothing, and C0's received pair differs from what was typed.

probes.name: PA3
probes.subject: tools/goal_template.py
probes.note: 🔴 The s295 vacuous PASS, reproduced: C1's --pattern restored to repr hands absent.py the translate pattern with a doubled backslash, which reads matched=0 on a file where the author's pattern matched once.

probes.name: PA4
probes.subject: tools/goal_template.py
probes.note: C1's --control restored to repr, on the value holding both quote kinds. repr escapes the inner single quote with a backslash, which bash does not honour inside single quotes, so the script dies on unbalanced quoting before absent.py runs and no evidence file exists.

probes.name: PA5
probes.subject: tools/goal_template.py
probes.note: 🔴 The second s295 shape: PA3's mutation on the escaped-paren pattern. Doubled, it is not a valid regex, so absent.py exits 2 and never writes the evidence file the judge is told to read.

probes.name: PA6
probes.subject: tools/goal_template.py
probes.note: C1's --file interpolated bare, as every file path was before this fix. The subject's directory carries a space and a quote, so bash splits and unbalances the argument.

probes.name: PA7
probes.subject: tools/goal_template.py
probes.note: A plausible wrong fix: wrap in single quotes without escaping. repr survived the single-quote case by switching to double quotes, so this is the mutation that gives that case teeth; the first embedded quote ends the argument, and C0 is the first script to hit it.

probes.name: PA8
probes.subject: tools/goal_template.py
probes.note: The other plausible wrong fix: no quoting at all, which is what T-COUNT and every file path had. C0 is the first script to run, so C0's pair is the claim it reddens.

probes.name: PA9
probes.subject: tools/goal_template.py
probes.note: 🔴 C0 loses --expect-present. Every value still arrives byte for byte, so both received-pair assertions stay green; only the exit code changes, and the exit code is the one thing the Stop gate records.

probes.name: PO0
probes.subject: tools/probe_battery/_battery.py
probes.note: Report-producer control: the driver's claim line stops naming the stable_key, so no pattern can tell the two banked reports apart. The control has to be able to go RED before C2's two readings mean anything.

probes.name: PO1
probes.subject: tools/goal_template.py
probes.note: C2's --pattern restored to repr. The escaped key's backslashes double, every alternative now demands a literal backslash the report does not contain, and the report that DOES credit the claim reads FAIL.

probes.name: PO2
probes.subject: tools/goal_template.py
probes.note: 🔴 The T-ORACLE defect (s295 M3): re.escape dropped. The crediting report still passes through the test_x branch, so on_credited stays green, and the report crediting a DIFFERENT claim passes too, through the #0 branch alone.

probes.name: PO3
probes.subject: tools/goal_template.py
probes.note: C2's --file interpolated bare. The banked report's directory has a space, so absent.py is handed two arguments and exits 2 on its own usage error, which is what the pre-fix renderer read.

probes.name: PC0
probes.subject: tools/tally.py
probes.note: Instrument control: tally's report line naming the field changes shape, so the argv-with-no-shell run can no longer be read back. A repr-style change would NOT do here: repr of the field prints the same quotes the parser already expects.

probes.name: PC1
probes.subject: tools/goal_template.py
probes.note: C0's --expect, with its appended impossible value, interpolated bare: the value with a space splits, and tally refuses its own argv before reading a record.

probes.name: PC2
probes.subject: tools/goal_template.py
probes.note: C1's --expect interpolated bare: the same split, on the reading itself. C0 stays quoted, so C0's assertion is green and the RED lands on C1's.

probes.name: PC3
probes.subject: tools/goal_template.py
probes.note: 🔴 The T-COUNT sibling as measured in s295: C1's --field interpolated bare, so a field with a space reaches tally as two arguments (unrecognized arguments: kind) and the check exits 2.

probes.name: PC4
probes.subject: tools/goal_template.py
probes.note: C0 loses --expect-refusal. Every value is unchanged and both received assertions stay green; C0 now reports its refused reading as a FAIL instead of passing as the control, and only the exit-code assertion can see that.
